_meta.description: Disease class -> treatment lookup for rice in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Structured data, not model output: the classifier decides WHAT the lesion is, this table decides what to DO about it. Nothing here is generated by an LLM. Chemical treatments and doses are always hand-curated from the sources below, never model output. A few entries' cultural-practice guidance (marked guidance_source: ai_general_non_chemical) was drafted by an LLM under a strict rule never to name a chemical or a dose, as a stopgap until reviewed; see review_note.
sources: ICAR-NRRI Cuttack - integrated pest and disease management for rice
IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank - rice disease management
Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee (CIB&RC), India - registered pesticide list
Uttar Pradesh Department of Agriculture - plant protection package of practices
_meta.review_note: Chemical names, doses and pre-harvest intervals must be re-checked against the current CIB&RC registered list, and against the UP plant protection package of practices, before any real farmer sees them. Treat this file as reviewed reference data, not as final agronomic advice. Entries marked guidance_source: ai_general_non_chemical also need their cultural-practice guidance reviewed by an agronomist, and ideally a hand-curated chemical_treatment added to replace the KVK referral.

healthy.label: Healthy
cultural_practice: No action needed. Continue routine monitoring.
Re-photograph in 7 days, or sooner if you see new spots.
healthy.notes: A healthy classification is not a guarantee the field is disease-free - it only describes the leaf in this photo.

brown_spot.label: Brown Spot

chemical_treatment.timing: At first appearance; repeat after 12-15 days if lesions continue to spread

cultural_practice: Brown spot is strongly associated with potassium and silicon deficiency - check the fertilizer plan before spraying again.
Avoid prolonged water stress; the disease worsens in under-irrigated fields.
Use certified, treated seed next season.
brown_spot.notes: Recurring brown spot usually signals a soil nutrition problem rather than a fungicide problem. Spraying alone will not fix a potassium-deficient field.

leaf_blast.label: Rice Leaf Blast

chemical_treatment.timing: At first lesion appearance, and again at panicle initiation if pressure persists

cultural_practice: Stop or reduce nitrogen top-dressing - excess nitrogen makes blast substantially worse.
Maintain a thin standing water layer; alternate wetting and drying raises blast risk.
Blast spreads fastest in cool nights with long leaf wetness - inspect daily during such weather.
leaf_blast.notes: Leaf blast can progress to neck blast at flowering, which is far more damaging to yield. Early action matters more than for any other disease in this list.

hispa.label: Rice Hispa
hispa.pathogen: Dicladispa armigera (insect pest, not a fungus)

chemical_treatment.application: Foliar spray targeting the leaf whorl
chemical_treatment.timing: When more than 1 adult per hill or heavy leaf scraping is visible

cultural_practice: Clip and destroy heavily damaged leaf tips before spraying - this removes most of the eggs and grubs.
Hand-collect adults early morning when they are sluggish; effective on small plots.
Avoid excess nitrogen, which encourages the lush growth hispa prefers.
hispa.notes: This is an insect, so a fungicide will do nothing. Getting the class right matters more here than the dose.

bacterial_leaf_blight.label: Bacterial Leaf Blight
cultural_practice: Plant resistant rice varieties to reduce bacterial leaf blight impact.
Remove and destroy infected plant debris to prevent disease spread.
Ensure proper field drainage to avoid waterlogging and reduce disease risk.
No chemical product or dose is listed for this disease in FarmSense yet - confirm chemical options with your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), Gorakhpur.
bacterial_leaf_blight.notes: This is a bacterial disease, so fungicides will not control it. Cultural-practice guidance above is AI-drafted (no chemical names or doses) and has not had agronomic review; severity is provisional.

tungro.label: Rice Tungro
tungro.pathogen: Rice tungro viruses (spread by leafhopper insects)
cultural_practice: Plant resistant rice varieties to reduce tungro virus impact.
Regularly inspect fields for green leafhoppers and remove them manually.
Maintain proper water levels to discourage leafhopper breeding.
No chemical product or dose is listed for this disease in FarmSense yet - confirm chemical options with your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), Gorakhpur.
tungro.notes: This is a virus, so fungicides will not control it. Cultural-practice guidance above is AI-drafted (no chemical names or doses) and has not had agronomic review; severity is provisional.

below_gate.message_ne: तस्बिर स्पष्ट नभएकोले निश्चित निदान गर्न सकिएन, त्यसैले कुनै उपचार सिफारिस गरिएको छैन।
actions: Take another photo in daylight, filling the frame with a single affected leaf.
Hold the phone steady about 15-20 cm from the leaf; avoid shadows and background clutter.
If the next photo is also inconclusive, contact your local agriculture extension officer (Krishi Vigyan Kendra, Gorakhpur).
